Surface Prep Unit Conversion

Surface characteristics prep for AERSURFACE

Land cover, Auer urban/rural, wet/dry/average moisture, and snow cover by month — packaged for an AERSURFACE run, not a replacement for one

What this tool does and doesn't do: it samples NLCD land cover around a site, applies the Auer method's radius/threshold rule for an urban/rural call, and builds month-by-month wet/dry/average moisture and snow-cover classifications from GHCN-Daily station history. It does not compute final AERSURFACE surface roughness, albedo, or Bowen ratio values — those come from AERSURFACE's own lookup tables applied to a full-resolution NLCD raster clip, which is what running the actual EPA AERSURFACE tool does (step 2 below can download that raster clip for you). See for exactly what's live-fetched, from where, and its limitations — this tool needs an internet connection at run time, unlike the other tools on this site.

1. Site location

Click the map, or drag the marker, to move the site.

2. Land cover

Samples a grid of points from MRLC's NLCD web service across the circle above and tallies land cover class by point — a statistical estimate of area composition, not an exact pixel-count integration. The land cover layer (year and region) is chosen automatically from the site's location. The download button fetches the actual classified raster (GeoTIFF, same NLCD layer) clipped to a square bounding the circle, ready to hand to the real AERSURFACE tool.

3. Auer urban/rural determination

The Auer (1978) method used throughout Appendix W dispersion modeling classifies a site as urban if more than 50% of the land within a 3 km radius falls in an Auer urban land-use category (heavy/light industrial, commercial, or compact/high-density residential); otherwise rural. This tool approximates those categories with NLCD's Developed, Medium Intensity and Developed, High Intensity classes (50–100% impervious surface) as a disclosed proxy, not an official EPA crosswalk — see the notes for why that's an imperfect substitute for actual land-use interpretation.

4. Precipitation & snow station

Nearest GHCN-Daily station with at least a 30-year precipitation record extending into the last few years is selected by default, but the nearest station is often not the most representative one — pick a different one from the list or by search. Snow depth (SNWD) reporting is shown separately from precipitation because many stations stopped reporting it years ago even though they still report precipitation; if your selected station has no current SNWD, pick a nearby one that does for step 7.

Finding nearest station…

5. Climatology baseline

Monthly precipitation totals for the period below are pulled live from NOAA NCEI to build each calendar month's 30th/70th percentile thresholds.

6. Meteorological processing year(s)

Add each year you're preparing AERMET/AERSURFACE inputs for.

7. Moisture regime and snow cover by month

Each added year's monthly precipitation total is compared against the baseline thresholds from step 5. Snow cover is the percentage of days each month with snow depth (SNWD) greater than zero at the selected station, fetched at daily resolution for the processing years only (not the full baseline) since it's a per-year classification, not a percentile one.

8. AERSURFACE prep summary

Site definition, land cover composition, Auer determination, station citations, and the moisture/snow regime by month, formatted to paste into your AERSURFACE run documentation. The 5-season month assignment AERSURFACE itself uses (lush vegetation, harvested cropland, late autumn, winter with snow, transitional spring) is climate- and judgment-dependent and is deliberately left for you to fill in here rather than defaulted.

Work through steps 1-7 above to build this summary.

Before this goes in a permit submission

  • Run the actual AERSURFACE tool against the downloaded (or a full-resolution) NLCD clip to get the roughness/albedo/Bowen ratio values themselves; this page does not compute them.
  • Confirm the precipitation and snow station(s) are climatologically representative of the site, not just the nearest ones with a long enough record — that judgment is why step 4 shows a list, not just one.
  • The land cover sample and the Auer determination are both statistical estimates from point sampling (see the sample counts shown); a small or clustered sample can misrepresent the true composition, especially near land cover boundaries.

Sources & data notes

Land cover: sampled live, per site, from MRLC's public NLCD web map/coverage service (mrlc.gov/geoserver), via point queries (WMS GetFeatureInfo) for the sampling in steps 2–3, and via WCS GetCoverage for the GeoTIFF download in step 2, not a bulk download in either case. Layer is chosen by the site's location: NLCD_2021_Land_Cover_L48 for the continental US, NLCD_2016_Land_Cover_AK for Alaska, NLCD_2001_Land_Cover_HI for Hawaii, NLCD_2001_Land_Cover_PR for Puerto Rico — Hawaii and Puerto Rico have not had a newer NLCD release as of this build. Sites outside all four coverage areas (e.g. the US Virgin Islands) have no NLCD layer available here at all; the tool says so rather than guessing. Each sample point is an independent live query; the reported composition is (points of class X) / (total points), a statistical estimate whose precision improves with the sample count you set in step 2, not an exact area integration of the underlying 30 m raster. The downloaded GeoTIFF is the actual classified raster at (approximately) native 30 m resolution, not a sample.

Auer urban/rural: the 3 km radius and 50% threshold are the documented Auer/Appendix W rule. The urban land-use categories Auer defined (heavy/light industrial, commercial, compact/high-density residential) were originally interpreted from aerial photography, not from land cover data, and no official EPA table crosswalks them to NLCD classes. This tool's substitution of NLCD Developed Medium + High Intensity for "Auer urban" is a reasonable, disclosed proxy, not an official determination: a dense low-rise commercial strip that reads as NLCD "Developed, Low Intensity" would be missed, for example. Treat the result as a starting point for the determination, not the determination itself, especially near the 50% line.

Precipitation and snow stations: the station list is NOAA NCEI's GHCN-Daily station inventory (ghcnd-stations.txt/ghcnd-inventory.txt), filtered at build time to stations with a PRCP period of record spanning at least 30 years and extending to within the last 3 years of the build date. SNWD (snow depth) period of record is shown independently per station and is not part of that filter, since it is commonly shorter or absent even at long-running PRCP stations. Neither is a completeness guarantee — a station can still have gap days or months inside its stated range; gaps show up as missing values in the fetched series rather than being silently filled in. Monthly precipitation totals are fetched live from NOAA NCEI's Global Summary of the Month (GSOM) service; daily snow depth is fetched live from the daily-summaries service for the processing years only.

Wet/dry/average classification: for each calendar month, the 30th and 70th percentiles of that month's total precipitation across all years in the baseline period are computed (linear interpolation between ranks). A processing year's month is Dry if its total is at or below the 30th percentile threshold, Wet if at or above the 70th percentile threshold, and Average otherwise.

Snow cover: for each processing year's month, the percentage of days with a reported snow depth greater than zero. This tool does not itself decide "winter with snow" vs. "winter, no snow" for AERSURFACE purposes — it reports the day-count and percentage so you can, alongside the moisture classification, which is a separate axis (a month can be snow-covered and also classified Wet, Dry, or Average by precipitation).

What is not done here: no roughness length, albedo, or Bowen ratio value is computed — those require AERSURFACE's own lookup tables applied to land cover within directional sectors from a full raster clip, and this tool does not reproduce that computation or its tables. No terrain or canopy height analysis is performed. Coordinates and station data are used as published; neither NLCD nor GHCN-Daily guarantee currency at every site.
